page: Microsoft Azure L128as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance within the Lasv5 series, built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD processor architecture and features 128 dedicated vCPUs. It is configured with 1024.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual core. Hardware acceleration via dedicated GPUs is not included on this instance type.

A central component of the L128as_v5 hardware profile is its high-capacity bundled local storage. The virtual machine includes 30,720 GB of direct-attached NVMe solid-state storage. In addition to local NVMe capacity, the instance supports Azure Premium Storage for external managed disk configurations. Networking provisions do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated virtual network provisioning or allocated IP resources for external routing.

From an architectural standpoint, the allocation of dedicated vCPUs alongside massive NVMe storage and substantial memory density provides predictable throughput for high-concurrency operations. Resource efficiency is centered on consolidation, allowing organizations to avoid multi-instance orchestration overhead for workloads requiring both extensive memory capacity and vast, low-latency local block storage.

The hardware configuration makes the L128as_v5 well-matched for large-scale transactional databases, distributed NoSQL engines such as Cassandra and MongoDB, data warehousing, large-scale search index nodes, and big data analytics pipelines that demand rapid local I/O combined with terabyte-scale RAM.
